title: Number of Unique Good Subsequences
summary: Given a binary string binary, determine the number of unique good subsequences.
statement: Given a binary string binary, determine the number of unique good subsequences. A good subsequence is defined as a non-empty sequence that does not have leading zeros, except for the single character "0". Calculate this count modulo 10^9 + 7. For example, if binary is "001", the good subsequences are "0", "0", and "1". The unique good subsequences are "0" and "1". Note that subsequences like "00", "01", and "001" are not considered good because they contain leading zeros.
constraints: binary has 1 through 100000 zero and one characters.
A good subsequence has no leading zero unless it is exactly "0"; equal resulting strings count once.
Return the number of distinct good nonempty subsequences modulo 1000000007.
hints: Track distinct valid subsequences by their final character rather than storing the strings.
Reading one replaces the set ending in one with every old valid nonzero sequence plus "1"; reading zero similarly appends zero, while standalone zero is tracked once.
Update end1=end0+end1+1 on one, end0=end0+end1 on zero, then add has_zero.
Appending the current digit groups results by their unique prefix and last digit; replacement removes duplicates created by later equal digits.
editorial: Appending the current digit groups results by their unique prefix and last digit; replacement removes duplicates created by later equal digits.
